s: The 23rd Law Commission of India is which kind of body?
x: The Law Commission is an executive body, neither constitutional nor statutory, advising the Ministry of Law and Justice.

s: Who is the full-time chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission?
x: Justice Dinesh Maheshwari has been full-time chair since 15 April 2025; the term runs to 31 August 2027.

s: Which of the following is included in the current mandate of the 23rd Law Commission?
x: The 23rd Law Commission's mandate includes examining a Uniform Civil Code; its recommendations are not binding.

s: At what level did the 16th Finance Commission keep the States' share of the divisible pool?
x: The 16th FC kept vertical devolution at 41%, the same as the 15th FC, and declined demands for 50%.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission award:
1. It keeps the States' share of the divisible pool at 41%.
2. It raises the weight of income distance to 45%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: income distance was cut to 42.5% from 45%.

s: Which criterion was newly introduced by the 16th Finance Commission for sharing taxes among States?
x: Contribution to GDP is the new criterion; the other three were already used and only had their weights changed.

s: Who chairs the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC, a constitutional body under Article 280, with an award period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s: Who has been the Chairperson of the Press Council of India since 24 April 2026?
x: Former SC judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai has chaired the PCI since 24 April 2026 for three years.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Press Council of India?
o: It is a statutory, autonomous and quasi-judicial body.
It is headquartered in New Delhi.
It has a Chairperson and 28 members.
It is a constitutional body created under Article 19(1)(a).
x: The PCI is statutory, under the Press Council Act, 1978; Article 19(1)(a) only guarantees press freedom.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council of India:
1. It has 13 journalist members among its 28 members.
2. It has 5 Members of Parliament: 3 from Lok Sabha and 2 from Rajya Sabha.
3. National Press Day is observed on 16 November.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the PCI has 13 journalists, 6 owners, 5 MPs, 3 institutional nominees and 1 news agency member; National Press Day is 16 November.

s: The Telangana Senior Citizens Commission has one Chief Commissioner and how many Commissioners?
x: The Commission has 1 Chief Commissioner (Justice E. Tirumala Devi) and 2 Commissioners.

s: Who chooses the Chairperson of the Press Council of India?
o: President on the advice of the Prime Minister
Chief Justice of India and Law Minister
Rajya Sabha Chairman, Lok Sabha Speaker and one PCI member
x: The PCI Chairperson is chosen by a panel of the RS Chairman, LS Speaker and one member of the Council.

s: Which report of the Law Commission of India recommended retaining the sedition provision (Section 124A of the IPC)?
x: The 22nd Law Commission's 279th Report, 'Usage of the Law of Sedition' (2023), recommended retaining Section 124A.

s: What did the Law Commission's 279th Report (2023) recommend on sedition?
o: Retain Section 124A with safeguards and higher punishment
Make sedition a bailable civil wrong
x: It said to keep Section 124A, add the Kedar Nath Singh (1962) safeguards and raise the punishment.

s: What weight did the 16th Finance Commission give to income distance in its formula for sharing taxes among States?
x: The 16th FC cut the weight of income distance from 45% to 42.5%; population (2011) got 17.5% and demographic performance 10%.

s: Which of the following can the Press Council of India NOT do?
x: PCI can warn, admonish and censure but cannot impose criminal penalties.

s: What is the award period of the 16th Finance Commission?
x: The 16th FC (Arvind Panagariya) covers 2026-27 to 2030-31.

s: When was NITI Aayog set up?
x: NITI Aayog, an executive body, was set up on 1 January 2015.

s: Under which Sections of the Press Council Act, 1978 did the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting nominate 13 journalists to the 15th Press Council of India in October 2026?
x: On 17 October 2026 the MIB nominated 13 journalists (six editors and seven working journalists) under Sections 5 and 6 of the Press Council Act, 1978.

s: Under the Press Council Act of which year was the Press Council of India first set up in 1966?
x: The PCI was first set up in 1966 under the Press Council Act, 1965; it can only warn, admonish or censure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 15th Press Council of India?
o: It has a Chairperson and 28 members.
Its members include 5 MPs: 3 from Lok Sabha and 2 from Rajya Sabha.
Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is its Chairperson since 24 April 2026.
National Press Day is observed on 26 November.
x: National Press Day is observed on 16 November, not 26 November; the other statements are correct.

s: Who has been appointed Chief Commissioner of the Telangana Senior Citizens Commission in October 2026?
x: Justice E. Tirumala Devi, a retired High Court judge, is the Chief Commissioner for three years.

s: What salary deduction do government employees neglecting their parents face under Telangana's new senior citizens framework?
x: A 15% salary deduction, credited to the parents, applies to government employees who neglect them.

s: Who heads the 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026?
x: Sanjay Jaiswal chairs the 31-member JPC (21 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the JPC on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026?
o: 21 members are from the Lok Sabha.
The nodal ministry for the FCRA is the Ministry of Finance.
10 members are from the Rajya Sabha.
x: The nodal ministry for the FCRA is the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance.

s: Which description correctly characterises a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
o: It is an executive committee that continues until dissolved by the President.
It is a permanent committee comprising members of only the Lok Sabha.
It is an ad hoc committee comprising members of both Houses and ends after completing its task.
It is a judicial committee comprising members of only the Rajya Sabha.
x: A Joint Parliamentary Committee is ad hoc, includes members of both Houses, and ends after completing its task. The other descriptions wrongly make it permanent, executive, judicial or limited to one House.

s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
x: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla named D. Purandeswari to chair the 31-member JPC (21 LS + 10 RS) on the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025. Sanjay Jaiswal chairs the FCRA 2026 JPC, Aparajita Sarangi the 130th Amendment JPC and Jagdambika Pal the Waqf JPC.

s: How many members does the JPC on the One Nation One Election (129th Amendment) Bill have?
x: The ONOE JPC under P.P. Chaudhary has 39 members: 27 Lok Sabha and 12 Rajya Sabha.

s: Which MP chaired the JPCs on both the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026 and the Biological Diversity Amendment Bill, 2021?
x: Sanjay Jaiswal chaired both JPCs; P.P. Chaudhary chaired the ONOE and Personal Data Protection JPCs.

s: Which of the following pairs (Bill – JPC chair) is correctly matched?
o: Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 – Jagdambika Pal
Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019 – Bhupender Yadav
Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Bill, 2022 – Rajendra Agrawal
x: Aparajita Sarangi chairs the 130th Amendment JPC; the Corporate Laws, PDP and Multi-State Cooperative JPCs were chaired by Sudheer Gupta, P.P. Chaudhary and C.P. Joshi.

s: Which Article of the Constitution lets each House of Parliament make its own rules of procedure?
x: Article 118 empowers each House to make its own rules of procedure.

s: Who chaired the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024?
x: The JPC on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was chaired by Jagdambika Pal.

s: Who chairs the JPC on the One Nation One Election (129th Constitution Amendment) Bill, 2024?
x: The 39-member JPC on the ONOE Bills is chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.

s: Who chaired the JPC on the Forest Conservation Amendment Bill, 2023?
x: Rajendra Agrawal chaired the JPC on the Forest Conservation Amendment Bill, 2023.

s: Who chaired the JPC on the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019?
x: P.P. Chaudhary chaired the PDP Bill 2019 JPC, and also the ONOE JPC.

s: What is the tenure of a Departmentally-Related Standing Committee (DRSC)?
x: DRSCs are standing committees with tenure up to one year; a JPC is ad hoc and ends after its task.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the DRSCs reconstituted for 2026-27?
o: Ministers can be members of these committees.
They examine Demands for Grants, bills and annual reports.
Eight of them work under the Rajya Sabha Chairman.
x: Ministers cannot be members of DRSCs.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on Finance for 2026-27?
x: Bhartruhari Mahtab heads Finance; Shashi Tharoor heads External Affairs and Radha Mohan Singh heads Defence.

s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:
1. A Joint Parliamentary Committee is ad hoc and ends after its task.
2. A Departmentally-Related Standing Committee is a standing committee with tenure up to one year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: a JPC is ad hoc, while a DRSC is a standing committee with tenure up to one year.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on External Affairs for 2026-27?
x: Shashi Tharoor chairs the External Affairs DRSC.

s: How many members does each Department-Related Standing Committee (DRSC) reconstituted for 2026-27 have?
x: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha.

s: Who chairs the Department-Related Standing Committee on Defence for 2026-27?
x: Radha Mohan Singh heads the Defence committee; Bhartruhari Mahtab heads Finance and Shashi Tharoor heads External Affairs.

s: Of the 24 DRSCs reconstituted in October 2026, how many work under the Lok Sabha Speaker?
x: 16 DRSCs work under the Lok Sabha Speaker and 8 under the Rajya Sabha Chairman.

s: Suresh N. Patel, Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, earlier held which post?
o: MD and CEO of Indian Bank
x: Suresh N. Patel is a former CVC, not an RBI official.

s: Which serving RBI Deputy Governor is a member of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat?
x: Shirish Chandra Murmu (RBI Deputy Governor) is a member; N.S. Vishwanathan is a former Deputy Governor.

s: Which body constituted the committee to curb unethical marketing in the pharma sector in October 2026?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: It was set up by the Department of Pharmaceuticals (Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers) and is headed by NITI Aayog Member M. Srinivas.

s: Which code guides ethical marketing practices in the pharmaceutical sector?
x: The Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices, 2024 guides ethical marketing; DPCO-2013 governs prices.

s: The Hockey India League, launched in 2013, was revived in which year after a seven-year break?
x: HIL began in 2013 and was revived in 2024 after a seven-year break.

s: Who chairs the RBI's Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets, announced on 4 November 2026?
o: RBI Deputy Governor in charge of Financial Markets Regulation
x: The committee is chaired by the RBI Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department.

s: Which markets does the RBI's Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (November 2026) cover?
o: Money, government securities, forex and related derivatives markets
x: Its remit is the RBI-regulated money, G-sec, foreign exchange and related derivatives markets and their infrastructure.

s: When was the Reserve Bank of India established?
x: RBI was set up on 1 April 1935; its HQ is Mumbai.

s: Who set up the seven-member committee to revive the Hockey India League in October 2026?
x: The committee to revive the Hockey India League was set up by Mansukh Mandaviya.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hockey India League and related bodies?
o: The Hockey India League began in 2013.
It was revived in 2024 after seven years.
Hockey India was set up in 2013.
FIH was founded in 1924 and is headquartered in Lausanne.
x: Hockey India was set up in 2009, not 2013; the other statements are correct.

s: Who heads the committee formed by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in October 2026 to curb unethical marketing in the pharma sector?
x: The committee is headed by M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog; Preeti Sudan and Naresh Trehan are members.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about pharma-sector bodies?
o: The Department of Pharmaceuticals was established in 2008 under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
The NPPA was set up in 1997.
The NPPA fixes drug prices under DPCO-2013.
The committee on unethical pharma marketing must report within six months of its first meeting.
x: The committee must report within two months of its first meeting, not six; the other statements are correct.

s: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) regulates drug prices under which order?
x: The NPPA, established in 1997 with headquarters in New Delhi, regulates prices under DPCO-2013.

s: Who is the Chairman of the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat set up on 30 October 2026?
x: Suresh N. Patel, former CVC, is the Chairman; Shirish Chandra Murmu and N. S. Vishwanathan are members.

s: Within what period must the High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, set up on 30 October 2026, give its roadmap?
x: The committee was set up on 30 October 2026 with a six-month deadline for its roadmap.

s: In which year was the Lead Bank Scheme introduced?
x: The Lead Bank Scheme dates from 1969; the RBI was established on 1 April 1935.

s: In which year was the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) established?
x: The NPPA was set up in 1997; the Department of Pharmaceuticals came in 2008.

s: What was the foodgrain production target for 2026–27 announced by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan?
x: The foodgrain production target for 2026–27 was fixed at 373.93 million tonnes. The figure of 376.56 million tonnes refers to the record production in 2025–26, while 177.72 million tonnes is the Rabi target.

s: What is the principal cereal of Kharif crops, which are sown with the southwest monsoon?
x: Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and rice is their main cereal; wheat is the main Rabi cereal.

s: NCRB's Crime in India 2024 (May 2026) is the first full-year data under which law?
x: Crime in India 2024 is the first full-year data under the BNS, 2023.

s: By how much did cybercrime rise as per NCRB's Crime in India 2024?
x: Cybercrime rose about 17.9%, while total cognisable crime fell about 6%.

s: Which organisation conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)?
x: PLFS is by the NSO under MoSPI; NFHS is coordinated by IIPS Mumbai.

s: Which body alone coordinated NFHS-6 (2023-24) for the first time?
x: NFHS-6, by the Health Ministry, was the first round coordinated solely by IIPS Mumbai.

s: Which of the following pairs (survey – conducting agency) is correctly matched?
x: ASER is by Pratham, an NGO; PLFS is by NSO (MoSPI) and NFHS-6 by the Health Ministry through IIPS Mumbai.

s: What was the overall unemployment rate (15+, CWS) as per the PLFS bulletin for September 2026?
x: Unemployment was 5.0% (rural 4.2%, urban 6.9%); it was 5.2% in September 2025.

s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index (2026)?
x: Gujarat topped IFI 2026 with 56.6, followed by Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha.

s: In NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: AP ranked 8th (48.7) and was a Frontrunner, not a Top Performer.

s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026 for the second year?
x: Odisha topped the Fiscal Health Index 2026 again; Punjab came last.

s: The 2026-27 foodgrain target of 373.93 MT is lower than which 2025-26 record?
x: The 2026-27 target (373.93 MT) is slightly lower than the 2025-26 record of 376.56 MT.

s: Which body does NITI Aayog's October 2026 report on the care economy recommend setting up?
x: The report recommends a National Care Council, a National Care Qualification Framework and a National Caregiver Registry.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's overall rank in NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index 2026?
x: AP was 8th overall (score 48.7) and placed as a 'Frontrunner'; Gujarat topped.

s: Which organisation publishes the Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India (ADSI) report?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: ADSI is the companion report of NCRB's Crime in India; the 2024 edition recorded 1,70,746 suicides.

s: NFHS-6 (2023-24) covered all States and Union Territories except which State?
x: NFHS-6 surveyed about 6.8 lakh households in all States/UTs except Manipur.

s: Which body released the Fiscal Health Index 2026?
x: The Fiscal Health Index is published by NITI Aayog; its second edition (March 2026) placed Odisha at the top.

s: How many pillars and indicators does NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index 2026 use?
x: IFI 2026 uses 8 pillars and 84 indicators across 28 States and 8 UTs.

s: Which State was placed last in NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026?
x: Odisha topped and Punjab was last in FHI 2026.

s: In which year was the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly (NPHCE) launched?
x: NPHCE was launched in 2010-11.

s: Per the NITI Aayog report of October 2026, India's 60+ population will reach how many by 2050?
x: The report projects 347 million elderly by 2050 (about 20.8%), up from 149 million in 2022.

s: The NITI Aayog report on the elderly (October 2026) calls for training how many multi-skilled caregivers?
x: The report calls for funds to train 1.5 lakh multi-skilled caregivers.

s: On which date is the International Day of Older Persons observed?
x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about elderly welfare in India?
o: Under the 2007 Senior Citizens Act, a senior citizen is a person aged 65 years or above.
Section 23 of the 2007 Act allows certain property transfers to be declared void.
Article 41 of the Constitution is associated with elderly welfare.
The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.
x: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 defines a senior citizen as a person aged 60 years or above, not 65.

s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), launched in 2008, has how many national missions?
x: The NAPCC (2008) comprises eight national missions; SAPCCs operate at the State level.

s: Which State became the first to introduce a dedicated comprehensive elderly care bill?
x: Kerala became the first State with a dedicated comprehensive elderly care bill.

s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers which combination of forms of abuse in the context of Kerala Police’s ‘Speak Up’ task force?
o: Physical, financial and cyber abuse, but not sexual or verbal abuse
Only verbal, emotional and economic abuse
Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse
x: The PWDVA, 2005 covers physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse. The other options omit one or more of these forms or introduce a limitation not stated in the law’s identified scope.

s: What punishment does Kerala's proposed comprehensive elderly care law provide for violations?
x: The proposed law covers abuse, neglect and illegal property occupation, mandates registration of old-age homes and provides for jail and fines.

s: Which Gram Panchayat was described as India's first net-zero panchayat in the context of panchayat-level climate action?
o: Gram Sabha of a Scheduled Area
A Gram Panchayat in Uttar Pradesh
x: Bela Gram Panchayat in Maharashtra was described as India's first net-zero panchayat, with initiatives including more than 90,000 trees, solar panels and waste segregation. Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka were also associated with initiatives, but the named panchayat was Bela.

s: Which of the following is included among the subjects in the Eleventh Schedule relevant to Panchayat-level development?
x: Non-conventional energy is among the subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule. Foreign trade, national defence, and currency and coinage are not the subjects identified in the Eleventh Schedule fact.

s: Which legislation empowers the Gram Sabha to protect community resources in Scheduled Areas?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
x: The PESA Act, 1996 provides for the Gram Sabha's role in protecting community resources in Scheduled Areas. The other options concern national climate missions, birth and death registration, and lottery regulation respectively.

s: In the action plan for a drug-free India, what approach was emphasised regarding drug trafficking?
o: Targeting only State-level offenders through a three-tier NCORD
Targeting only small offenders through a two-tier NCORD
Targeting whole networks and supply chains, along with strengthening the four-tier NCORD
Targeting only international suppliers through a single-tier NCORD
x: The strategy emphasised targeting whole networks and supply chains rather than only small offenders, while strengthening the four-tier NCORD. The other options incorrectly narrow the target or change the NCORD structure.

s: At the high-level meeting in Panaji, Goa, what was the target year set in the action plan for a drug-free India?
x: The action plan aims to achieve a drug-free India by 2029. The year 2047 is associated with the broader Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, not the drug-free India target.

s: Which Article concerns devolution to Panchayats for economic development and social justice?
x: Article 243G concerns devolution for economic development and social justice; panchayat climate plans are integrated into the GPDP.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan – 2020; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Narcotics Control Bureau – 2020; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking – Directive Principle
x: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan began in 2020 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The NCB dates to 1986 (MHA), Article 47 is a Directive Principle, and the international day is June 26.

s: In which year was the Narcotics Control Bureau set up?
x: The NCB was set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Home Affairs to enforce the NDPS Act, 1985.

s: In which year was the National Commission for Women set up?
x: NCW was set up in 1992.

s: In which year was the NDPS Act enacted?
x: The NDPS Act dates from 1985; the NCB was set up in 1986.

s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment added which Part to the Constitution?
x: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX on Panchayats.

s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs, except for medicinal purposes?
x: Article 47 (a Directive Principle) asks the State to prohibit intoxicants injurious to health, except for medicinal use.

s: Which institution was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 October 2026 as a Special Purpose Vehicle for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring in the transport and logistics sector?
o: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan
x: The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) was approved as an SPV for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring. The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and National Logistics Policy are separate initiatives, while IWAI is associated with inland waterways.

s: Central projects of what cost are technically appraised by the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA)?
x: ITLA undertakes technical appraisal of central projects of ₹500 crore or more; it also prepares a 10+ year National Transport Master Plan.

s: Which top telecom decision-making body was abolished by the Centre after functioning for 37 years?
x: The Centre abolished the Digital Communications Commission, or DCC, which had served as the top telecom decision body for 37 years. Telecom Commission was its former name, while the Narco-Coordination Centre is a drug-control mechanism.

s: Who released the strategic action plan Mission Rangeen Machhli–2031 at Agatti, Lakshadweep?
x: The Vice-President released Mission Rangeen Machhli–2031 for ornamental fisheries at Agatti, Lakshadweep.

s: For whom is training meant under Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031?
o: Coastal fishers, youth and women SHGs
x: The Mission's training covers coastal fishers, youth and women self-help groups, not coastal fishers alone.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the RoDTEP scheme is incorrect?
o: It was notified by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.
RoDTEP replaced MEIS and is WTO-compliant.
The scheme became effective from 1 January 2021.
x: The incorrect statement is that RoDTEP was notified by the Department of Revenue through CBIC. It was notified by the Department of Commerce through DGFT; implementation is carried out by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.

s: RoDTEP, in force from 1 January 2021, replaced which export scheme?
x: RoDTEP replaced MEIS, which faced WTO objections; RoDTEP is WTO-compliant.

s: In which year was the Telecom Commission, later renamed the Digital Communications Commission, set up?
x: The Telecom Commission was set up in 1989 and renamed DCC in 2018; it was abolished after 37 years.

s: After the DCC was abolished, which body now examines telecom projects of ₹500-1,000 crore?
x: Projects of ₹500–1,000 crore go to the Expenditure Finance Committee; the Telecom Secretary approves up to ₹100 crore and the Minister up to ₹500 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RoDTEP scheme:
1. It is notified by the Department of Commerce through DGFT.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Revenue through CBIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: DGFT notifies RoDTEP and CBIC implements it, not the other way round.

s: Which plan, with a horizon of more than 10 years, will the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) prepare?
x: ITLA will prepare the National Transport Master Plan covering roads, rail, ports, aviation, waterways and logistics.

s: For which sector is Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031 a strategic action plan?
x: Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031 of the Department of Fisheries is for ornamental (colourful) fish.

s: Which department leads Mission Rangeen Machhli-2031, linked with PMMSY?
x: The Department of Fisheries leads it; it is linked with PMMSY.

s: In which year was the agreement behind the Pennaiyar water dispute between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka made?
x: The Pennaiyar dispute is linked to an 1892 agreement; Tamil Nadu sought a tribunal in November 2019.

s: The Union Home Minister proposed linking which river system sequence in the context of Interlinking of Rivers?
x: The proposal was to link rivers from the Brahmaputra to the Godavari and Cauvery. The Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar option is a separate link opposed by Kerala, not the Union Home Minister’s proposal.

s: In which year was the National Water Development Agency set up?
x: NWDA was set up in 1982; the National Perspective Plan (30 links) dates to 1980.

s: Which State opposed the Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar river-linking project over possible harm to the Vembanad wetland?
x: Kerala opposed the Pamba–Achankovil–Vaippar link, citing possible harm to the Vembanad wetland.

s: Which of the following pairs (project – detail) is correctly matched?
o: Krishna Water Supply – Water to Hyderabad
Indira Gandhi Canal – Periyar in Kerala to Vaigai in Tamil Nadu
x: The Krishna Water Supply project supplies water to Hyderabad. Mullaperiyar diverts Periyar to Vaigai, and the Indira Gandhi Canal takes Sutlej–Beas water to Rajasthan.

s: How many river links did the National Perspective Plan (1980) identify?
x: The NPP (1980) identified 30 links: 14 Himalayan and 16 Peninsular; NWDA came in 1982.

s: The idea of interlinking Indian rivers goes back to whom?
x: The idea goes back to Sir Arthur Cotton in the 19th century; NWDA was set up in 1982.

s: The Mullaperiyar project diverts water from which river to which?
x: Mullaperiyar takes Periyar (Kerala) water to the Vaigai (Tamil Nadu).

s: The first post-Independence international cargo voyage from Bogibeel Terminal travelled through which route to reach Pangaon Port in Dhaka?
o: PM Gati Shakti GIS platform and the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route
Dhubri–Sadiya route and the National Logistics Policy corridor
NW-2 on the Brahmaputra and the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route
Coastal waterways and the National Transport Master Plan route
x: The voyage followed NW-2 on the Brahmaputra and then the Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route to Pangaon Port, Dhaka. NW-2 extends from Dhubri to Sadiya and is associated with IWAI, but the other options do not describe the voyage route.

s: National Waterway-2 (Dhubri–Sadiya) on the Brahmaputra is how long?
x: NW-2 runs 891 km from Dhubri to Sadiya and is managed by IWAI.

s: Who flagged off the first post-Independence international cargo voyage from Bogibeel on 5 October 2026?
x: Sarbananda Sonowal flagged it off from Bogibeel Terminal, Dibrugarh; it carried methanol from APCL Namrup.

s: Which agency manages National Waterway-2 (Dhubri-Sadiya)?
x: NW-2 on the Brahmaputra is managed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI).

s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) on 4 November 2026?
x: Retired IAS officer Binoy Kumar succeeded P. Venkata Rama Reddy; term 5 years or till age 70.

s:
Consider the following about APERC:
1. It was set up on 31 March 1999 under the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Reform Act, 1998.
2. It consists of a Chairperson and two Members.
3. It is a constitutional body under Article 243.
Which of the above is/are correct?

x: Sarvam AI (Bengaluru, 2023) was founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the identification of Scheduled Tribes?
x: Under Article 342 the President specifies the Scheduled Tribes; Article 338A deals with the NCST.

s: The Vyomaa Innovation Challenge for offline multilingual voice AI was launched by which body?
x: Bhashini ran the Vyomaa Innovation Challenge with Current AI and Kalpa Impact; its device is 'Sunno Sutra'.

s: Which of the following statements about the PCPNDT Act and ultrasound machines is incorrect?
o: The law was enacted in 1994 as the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act.
A machine may be used at any location after it has been registered once.
Registration is required before purchasing ultrasound machines.
The 2003 amendment added pre-conception provisions and renamed it the PCPNDT (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act.
x: The incorrect statement is that a registered machine may be used at any location. The machine must stay at its registered location; registration is required before purchase and sex disclosure is prohibited.

s: Which of the following statements about India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine is incorrect?
o: African Swine Fever is a viral disease of pigs that infects humans.
It was developed by ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal.
It was dedicated by Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
It is the MA-104 Cell Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever Vaccine.
x: The incorrect statement is that African Swine Fever infects humans; the disease does not infect humans. The vaccine was developed by ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal, and was dedicated by Shivraj Singh Chouhan.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the FSSAI action against misleading food claims is incorrect?
o: FSSAI issued more than 150 notices concerning misleading advertisements, false claims and labelling.
In May 2025, FSSAI advised stopping the use of the expression “Energy Drink” on labels.
Mondelez India withdrew health and nutrient-comparison claims on Bournvita.
The action covered labels, advertisements, e-commerce listings and delivery platforms.
x: The second statement is incorrect: in May 2025 FSSAI advised stopping the use of "100%" on labels, not "Energy Drink". The other statements are correct: FSSAI issued 150+ notices covering labels, ads, e-commerce listings and delivery platforms, and Mondelez India withdrew health and nutrient-comparison claims on Bournvita.

s: Which institute developed India's first indigenous African Swine Fever vaccine?
x: The MA-104 cell-line vaccine was developed by ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal; ASF does not infect humans.

s: In which year was the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act enacted, later renamed the PCPNDT Act by a 2003 amendment?
x: The PNDT Act was enacted in 1994; the 2003 amendment added pre-conception techniques and renamed it the PCPNDT Act.

s: The High-Level Committee on demographic change linked to illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons was constituted by which authority?
x: The committee was constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs to study demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other abnormal reasons. The Inter-State Council and Finance Commission are separate constitutional bodies, while the Census Commissioner is a member of the committee.

s: In which case (2005) was illegal migration into Assam characterised as 'external aggression'?
x: The Sarbananda Sonowal case (2005) characterised illegal migration into Assam as external aggression.

s: The Madhukar Gupta Committee of 2016 is associated with which of the following?
o: The Union’s duty to protect States from external aggression
Protection of tribal land in the Santhal Pargana region
x: The Madhukar Gupta Committee of 2016 was associated with the Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS). The Assam Accord, tribal land protection and the Union’s protective duty arise from different legal or policy references.

s: To what level does the Education to Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee aim to raise India's share in the global services market by 2047?
x: The committee's goal is a 10% share in the global services market by 2047.

s: How many empowered teams did the Prime Minister announce on March 24, 2026, after a CCS review?
x: The Prime Minister announced seven empowered teams on March 24, 2026, following a CCS review.

s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on Demographic Change proposed in May 2026?
x: The High-Level Committee on Demographic Change was chaired by Justice Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar and dealt with demographic change arising from illegal immigration.

s: Which Article of the Constitution places a duty on the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
x: Article 355 sets the Union's duty to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance.

s: Who chairs the Education to Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee?
x: NITI Aayog CEO Nidhi Chhibber chairs it; its first meeting was on 22 May 2026.

s: Within what period must the High-Level Committee on demographic change submit its report?
x: The report is due within 1 year, extendable by 6 months.

s: What did the Lt. Gen. S.K. Sinha Report (1998) deal with?
o: Demographic change in border districts due to illegal migration
x: The S.K. Sinha Report (1998) flagged demographic change in border districts caused by illegal migration.

s: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 relates to which of the following?
o: National Register of Citizens in all States
x: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 was inserted to give effect to the Assam Accord.

s: What was India's Total Fertility Rate as per NFHS-5?
x: NFHS-5 put India's TFR at 2.0, cited in the context of the demographic change committee.

s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission (October 2022) examines extending SC status to Dalits converted to which religions?
x: The Commission examines SC status for Dalits who converted to Christianity and Islam.

s: Under Article 341, who specifies the Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory after consultation with the Governor?
o: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The President specifies the Scheduled Castes for each State or Union Territory after consulting the Governor. The SC list can be modified only by Parliament, so Parliament is not the authority that initially specifies it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation for Scheduled Castes?
o: Under Article 341, the President specifies SCs after consulting the Governor
The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 was originally for Hindus and later extended to Sikhs and Buddhists
Articles 330 and 332 provide reservation in legislatures
Reservation is provided for SCs in private-sector jobs
x: There is no reservation in private-sector jobs; the other three statements are correct.

s: Under Article 341, who alone can modify the list of Scheduled Castes?
x: The President notifies the SC list after consulting the Governor, but only Parliament can change it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950:
1. It originally covered Hindus only.
2. It was extended to Sikhs in 1956.
3. It was extended to Christians in 1990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1990 extension was to Buddhists; Christians and Muslims are not included.

s: The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission was notified by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
x: The Commission of Inquiry was notified by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

s: Who was the first Dalit Chief Justice of India?
x: K.G. Balakrishnan, the 37th CJI (2007-2010), was the first Dalit CJI; he now heads the commission on SC status of converts.

s: Who heads the Commission of Inquiry on extending Scheduled Caste status to Dalits who converted to Christianity and Islam?
x: The commission set up on 6 October 2022 is headed by former CJI K.G. Balakrishnan, India's first Dalit CJI.

s: Who heads the Lok Sabha Estimates Committee for 2026–27?
x: Dr. Sanjay Jaiswal heads the Estimates Committee; K.C. Venugopal heads the PAC.

s: Regarding parliamentary committees, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Estimates Committee – 22 members, 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha
Public Accounts Committee – Examines CAG reports
Committee on Public Undertakings – 30 members, Lok Sabha only
Committee on Privileges – Examines CAG reports
x: The PAC examines CAG reports; the Estimates Committee has 30 Lok Sabha members and the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 (15 LS + 7 RS).

s: Who chairs the Public Accounts Committee for 2026-27?
x: K.C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27, which examines CAG audit reports.

s: Who instituted the Sansad Ratna Awards?
x: The Sansad Ratna Awards were instituted by the Prime Point Foundation; the 2026 edition honoured 12 MPs.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vice-President and the Rajya Sabha?
o: The Vice-President is the ex officio Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Article 63 provides for a Vice-President of India
The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members
x: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, not the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

s: The Lok Sabha Estimates Committee for 2026-27 has how many members?
x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from Lok Sabha; PAC and COPU have 22 (15 + 7).

s: Which of the following pairs (committee – members) is correctly matched?
o: Committee on Public Undertakings – 30, Lok Sabha only
Welfare of SCs and STs – 22 (15 LS + 7 RS)
x: PAC and COPU have 22 (15 + 7); the Estimates Committee has 30 from Lok Sabha only; the SC/ST Welfare Committee has 30 (20 + 10).

s: Who chairs the Lok Sabha Committee on Privileges, the first under the 18th Lok Sabha?
x: Ravi Shankar Prasad chairs the Committee on Privileges with 14 other MPs.

s: Who chairs the Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026?
x: The Joint Committee on the Corporate Laws Amendment Bill, 2026 is chaired by Sudheer Gupta.

s: Who chairs the Lok Sabha Committee on Empowerment of Women constituted on 21 April 2026?
x: D. Purandeswari chairs the Committee on Empowerment of Women.

s: Who chairs the Rajya Sabha Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change from May 2026?
x: Medha Vishram Kulkarni was made its chair from 18 May 2026 under Rule 269.

s: Who chairs the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for 2026-27?
x: Faggan Singh Kulaste chairs the 30-member (20 LS + 10 RS) committee on Welfare of SCs and STs.

s: Who is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha House Committee?
x: Dr. K. Laxman chairs the Rajya Sabha House Committee, which handles members' accommodation and amenities.

s: Who chairs the Telangana Women’s Commission, which has a five-year term?
x: Gadwal Vijayalakshmi, formerly the GHMC Mayor, is the Chair of the Telangana Women’s Commission, whose term is five years. Vijaya Rahatkar chairs the NCW, Annapurna Devi is the WCD Minister, and Kasoju Shankaramma is a member of the Telangana commission.

s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under which Article?
x: The NCSC is under Article 338; the 89th Amendment (2003) split it from the NCST and the 65th Amendment (1990) made it multi-member.

s: The NCBC received constitutional status under Article 338B through which Amendment?
x: The NCBC became statutory in 1993 and constitutional in 2018 under Article 338B (102nd Amendment).

s: Which body was replaced by the National Dental Commission set up on 19 March 2026?
x: The National Dental Commission replaced the Dental Council of India, established in 1949.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment split the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into separate NCSC and NCST?
x: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission, creating separate constitutional commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

s: Who assumed office as Chairperson of the NCBC on 27 March 2026?
x: Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti replaced Hans Raj Gangaram Ahir as NCBC Chairperson.

s: Who was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in April 2026?
x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri replaced Suman Bery on 25 April 2026 and took charge on 8 May 2026.

s: Which of the following is an executive body, neither constitutional nor statutory?
x: The Law Commission is executive and advisory; NCSC, NCBC and the Finance Commission are constitutional.

s: Which Act was repealed when the National Dental Commission was set up in March 2026?
x: The National Dental Commission replaced the Dental Council of India and the Dentists Act, 1948 was repealed.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes a multi-member body?
x: The 65th Amendment (1990) made it multi-member; the 89th (2003) split it into NCSC and NCST.

s: Which factor is the 16th Finance Commission said to give weight to?
x: The 16th Finance Commission gives weight to contribution to GDP. The other options are demands for special constitutional or fiscal treatment mentioned in the federalism debate, not the stated criterion of the 16th Finance Commission.

s: Which of the following pairs consists of commissions on Centre-State relations?
o: Punchhi and All India Services Commission
x: The Sarkaria Commission and the Punchhi Commission are identified as commissions on Centre-State relations. The Finance Commission, All India Services and President’s Rule are subjects associated with constitutional provisions, not the two commissions asked about here.

s: Which constitutional provision assigns residuary powers to the Union in the context of Indian federalism?
x: Article 248 deals with residuary powers with the Union. Article 263 concerns the Inter-State Council, Article 280 the Finance Commission, and Article 356 President’s Rule.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian federalism?
o: S.R. Bommai (1994) held federalism to be part of the Basic Structure and curbed Article 356
Article 1(1) describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States'
In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023), the SC held that Governors may indefinitely delay assent to Bills
State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1962) described India as quasi-federal
x: The 2023 Punjab case held that Governors cannot indefinitely delay assent to Bills; the other three statements are correct.

s: Which case laid down the requirement of quantifiable data for conditions relating to promotion quota?
x: M. Nagaraj laid down the quantifiable-data requirement; Indra Sawhney prescribed the creamy layer for OBCs.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Inter-State Council?
x: Article 263 deals with the Inter-State Council; Article 280 is the Finance Commission, 356 President's Rule and 312 All India Services.

s: What term has been used to describe a Governor's delay in giving assent to Bills?
x: Gubernatorial delays in assent have been described as a pocket veto.

s: For which region was Sixth Schedule status demanded in the debate on Indian federalism?
x: Sixth Schedule status was sought for Ladakh, while Bihar and Odisha sought Special Category Status.

s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for Special Category Status under the Gadgil-Mukherjee framework?
o: High population density in urban areas
Low population density or a sizeable tribal population
x: The criterion is low population density or a sizeable tribal population, not high urban population density.

s: In which year was the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha membership removed?
x: The domicile requirement was removed in 2003; vertical devolution is formally 41%.

s: Of the 16th Finance Commission grants to Telangana's rural local bodies, what share goes to Gram Panchayats?
x: GPs get 80%, intermediate and district panchayats 10% each, of Telangana's ₹9,968 crore.

s: What share of the divisible pool goes to the States as vertical devolution under the 16th Finance Commission?
x: Vertical devolution is formally 41%; cesses and surcharges lie outside the divisible pool.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court apply the creamy layer exclusion to OBC reservation?
x: Indra Sawhney (1992) introduced the creamy layer for OBCs; M. Nagaraj asked for quantifiable data on promotion quota.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the All India Services?
x: Article 312 provides for the All India Services.

s: How many women MPs were there in the Lok Sabha in 2019?
x: Women MPs in the Lok Sabha numbered 78 in 2019.

s: The Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0 was released by which ministry for 2023–24 on National Panchayati Raj Day?
o: Ministry of Panchayati Raj and Ministry of Rural Development jointly
x: PAI 2.0 was released by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj for 2023–24 on National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April. The Ministry of Rural Development was not identified as the releasing ministry.

s: The Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0 is notable for being which of the following?
o: India’s first comprehensive data-driven framework to assess Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies
India’s first framework to assess State Finance Commissions
India’s first framework to rank National Panchayati Raj institutions
India’s first framework to assess only urban local bodies
x: PAI 2.0 is India’s first comprehensive data-driven framework for assessing Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies. The other options incorrectly limit or change the type of institutions assessed.

s: Which State did not participate in the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0?
x: West Bengal stayed out of PAI 2.0, while Tripura was the top State and Uttar Pradesh had the highest participation.

s: What is the main cause of death in stampedes?
x: Compressive asphyxia is the main cause of death in stampedes.

s: Which of the following is NOT a measure recommended in NDMA guidelines for preventing stampedes?
o: Real-time monitoring through CCTV and drones
Capacity mapping to keep crowds within safe limits
x: The NDMA recommends public address systems, so eliminating them is not a recommended measure.

s:
Arrange the following countries in chronological order of the grant of universal adult franchise:
1. India
2. Japan
3. Sri Lanka
4. United States of America
x: The correct order is United States of America in 1920, Sri Lanka in 1931, Japan in 1945 and India in 1950. Therefore, the sequence is 4-3-2-1.

s: As per NCRB Crime in India 2023, how many of the 180 cases of denial of access to public spaces to SCs were from Uttar Pradesh?
x: Uttar Pradesh accounted for 173 of the 180 cases in 2023.

s: Which country was the first to give women the right to vote, in 1893?
x: New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote, in 1893, associated with Kate Sheppard. The United States, Sri Lanka and Japan correspond to later stages in the stated sequence of universal adult franchise.

s: Which Directive Principle Article concerns the organisation of village panchayats?
x: Article 40 concerns organising village panchayats; Part IX and the 11th Schedule came from the 73rd Amendment.

s: Article 17, which abolishes untouchability, is part of which Fundamental Right?
x: Article 17 is part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18), not the Right to Freedom.

s:
Assertion (A): Section 4 of the SC/ST Act penalises officials’ neglect.
Reason (R): The Protection of Civil Rights Act was enacted in 1989.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true because Section 4 of the SC/ST Act penalises officials’ neglect. Reason R is false: the Protection of Civil Rights Act was enacted in 1955, while 1989 is associated with the SC/ST Act.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding women's representation in the Lok Sabha is incorrect?
o: Women MPs numbered 78 in 2019, the highest among the listed years.
x: The incorrect statement is that women MPs numbered 74 in 2014; the correct figure for 2014 was 62. The figure of 74 applied to 2024, while 2019 recorded the highest figure among these years at 78.

s: Who conducted the Women and Politics Survey (2019)?
x: The Lokniti-CSDS Women and Politics Survey (2019) found many women needed family permission to take part.

s: Which State topped the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0?
x: Tripura was the top State, with about 80% of its Panchayats as Front Runners; UP had the highest participation.

s: In which category did the largest number of Gram Panchayats fall under PAI 2.0?
x: Performer (B) was the largest group with 1,18,824 Panchayats (about 45.72%); no GP reached A+.

s: Which district has the highest cancer incidence in the Cancer Atlas of Telangana 2026?
x: Hanumakonda has the highest incidence (79 per lakh), followed by Hyderabad (72).

s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
x: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added the 11th Schedule with 29 subjects for Panchayats.

s: Which State recorded the highest participation in the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0, with all its 57,678 Gram Panchayats?
x: Uttar Pradesh had all 57,678 GPs assessed; Tripura was the top State in performance.

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment provided what under Articles 15(6) and 16(6)?
o: Reservation for SEBCs, SCs and STs
x: The 103rd Amendment of 2019 provided 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections under Articles 15(6) and 16(6). Reservation in promotion for SC/ST is associated with Article 16(4A), not these provisions.

s: Against whom, and by whom, does Article 15(1) prohibit discrimination?
x: Article 15(1) bars the State from discriminating against citizens; descent is not one of its listed grounds.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the BCCI?
o: It is substantially controlled and financed by the government.
It is a private society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975.
Zee Telefilms v. Union of India (2005) held it not to be 'State' under Article 12.
The CIC held in May 2026 that it is not a public authority under the RTI Act.
x: The BCCI is a private society not substantially controlled or financed by the government.

s: In its ruling of 18 May 2026, how did the Central Information Commission classify the BCCI under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, 2005?
o: It is a public authority only for cricket administration
It is a public authority in every respect
It is a security body exempt under Section 24
It is not a public authority
x: The Central Information Commission held on 18 May 2026 that the BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, 2005. The ruling did not classify the BCCI as a security body or as a public authority for cricket administration.

s: According to the Supreme Court ruling concerning the inclusion of Rajasthani in a teacher recruitment examination syllabus, what was recognised as part of the right to identity?
o: Thinking and expressing in one’s own language
Only instruction in a mother tongue at the primary stage
Only the preference for mother tongue under NEP 2020
Inclusion of every regional language in every teacher recruitment examination
x: The Supreme Court recognised that thinking and expressing in one’s language forms part of the right to identity. Article 350A concerns instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minority children, while NEP 2020 favours mother tongue; neither creates the broader claim in the other options.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the earlier CIC ruling on the BCCI is incorrect?
o: In 2018, the CIC held the BCCI to be a public authority.
The 2018 decision was given by Information Commissioner M. Sridhar Acharyulu.
The 2018 CIC holding declared that the BCCI was not a public authority.
The Madras High Court set aside the 2018 CIC holding.
x: The incorrect statement is that the 2018 CIC holding declared the BCCI not to be a public authority. The holding instead treated the BCCI as a public authority, and it was subsequently set aside by the Madras High Court.

s: What did the Law Commission’s 275th Report of 2018 recommend in relation to the BCCI?
o: Limiting RTI coverage to the BCCI’s e-sports activities
Exempting the BCCI from Article 226 review
Treating the BCCI as a security body under the Second Schedule
Bringing the BCCI under the RTI framework
x: The Law Commission’s 275th Report, issued in 2018, recommended that the BCCI be brought under the RTI framework. The other options do not state the recommendation associated with that report.

s: To what extent are government-funded sports bodies covered by RTI under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025?
o: Only to the extent of the government funds
Only in matters of corruption and human rights
x: Government-funded sports bodies are subject to RTI only to the extent of those funds; the corruption/human-rights exception applies to exempt security bodies.

s: Under the UGC Promotion of Equity in HEIs Regulations, 2026, which body functions as the nodal body in every institution?
x: The Regulations provide for an Equal Opportunity Centre as the nodal body in every higher educational institution.

s: Amid which concerns did the Supreme Court's interim stay on the UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions Regulations, 2026 come?
x: The context was caste discrimination and student suicides, including the Abeda Salim Tadvi case.

s: What kind of grievance system do the UGC Equity Regulations, 2026 provide for?
o: Only an online portal during working hours
A 24/7 system with helplines, portals, Equity Officers and Equity Squads
Complaints only through the State Government
x: The Regulations provide a 24/7 grievance system with helplines, portals, Equity Officers and Equity Squads.

s: Which clause of Article 15 enables special provisions for women and children?
x: Article 15(3) concerns special provisions for women and children; 15(4) covers SEBCs, SCs and STs and 15(5) educational institutions.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children of linguistic minorities?
x: Article 350A asks States to provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage to linguistic-minority children.

s: The Lodha Committee is associated with reforms in which body?
x: In BCCI v. Cricket Association of Bihar (2016) the Supreme Court backed the Lodha Committee reforms of the BCCI.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotion for SCs and STs?
x: The 77th Amendment (1995) inserted Article 16(4A); the 103rd (2019) gave 10% EWS reservation.

s: Under Section 24 of the RTI Act, information from exempted security organisations can still be sought on which matters?
x: Security bodies in the Second Schedule are exempt, except for information on corruption and human rights violations.

s: Which body functions under the Agriculture Ministry and classifies pesticides into four toxicity classes based on LD50?
x: CIBRC functions under the Agriculture Ministry and classifies pesticides into four toxicity classes by LD50. FSSAI sets MRLs, while the Central Pesticides Board and Registration Committee have separate roles under the pesticides framework.

s: With reference to the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025, identify the incorrect statement.
o: It replaces the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
It is administered under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
It provides for a Central Pesticides Board and a Registration Committee.
It includes bio-pesticides within its coverage.
x: The incorrect statement is that the Bill is administered under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. It is under the Ministry of Agriculture; the Bill replaces the specified insecticides law and rules, covers bio-pesticides, and provides for the Central Pesticides Board and Registration Committee.

s: Why was discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 deferred by the Union government?
o: A Supreme Court order relating to foreign contributions
Opposition concerns over minority-led institutions and civil society
The expiry of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010
A disagreement over the Consolidated Fund of India
x: Discussion on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was deferred after opposition concerns over minority-led institutions and civil society. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 is the parent Act, not the reason stated for the deferment.

s: What is the Designated Authority meant to do under the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026?
o: Take over and manage foreign contributions and assets of bodies whose registration is cancelled, surrendered or expired
Approve foreign contributions before they are received
Audit annual returns of FCRA-registered bodies
x: The Designated Authority takes over and manages the foreign contributions and assets of bodies whose registration has ceased.

s: What does the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026 do to restrictions on persons in news production and broadcasting?
x: The Bill expands, not removes, restrictions on persons in news production and broadcasting.

s: Which body sets the Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) for pesticides in India?
o: Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee
x: MRLs are set by FSSAI, not the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee.

s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 is under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
x: The Bill, replacing the Insecticides Act, 1968, is under the Agriculture Ministry, not Chemicals and Fertilizers.

s: Which Act will the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 replace?
x: The draft Bill replaces the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.

s: What did the NSE launch as a dedicated segment in May 2026?
x: NSE launched a dedicated segment for Electronic Gold Receipts, which are SEBI-regulated securities backed by physical gold in approved vaults. Unclaimed deposits, AIFs and maritime insurance are separate financial-sector developments.

s: Under SEBI’s GARUDA mechanism, the approval timeline for schemes of non-accredited investors is reduced from 30 to what number of working days?
x: GARUDA reduces the timeline for non-accredited investor schemes from 30 to 10 working days. The other periods are not specified as the revised GARUDA timeline.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Category III AIFs are hedge funds; Category I covers startups and Category II private equity, and SEBI (set up 1988) got statutory status in 1992.

s: Which organisation has been designated as the PaRRVA Agency for verifying past risk and return claims?
x: CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency, while NSE serves as the PaRRVA Data Centre. PaRRVA verifies performance claims of advisers, research analysts and algo providers.

s: Which entities collaborated to detect and freeze mule accounts through an MoU-related initiative?
x: I4C and the RBI Innovation Hub collaborated to detect and freeze mule accounts. The RBI Innovation Hub was established in Bengaluru in 2022, while I4C was established in 2018 under the MHA; EPFO and MoSPI are not the partners identified for this initiative.

s: Why was SEBI's Cyber-suraksha.ai Task Force (May 2026) set up?
x: The task force deals with AI-driven cyber threats; Sudarshan tracks finfluencers, PaRRVA verifies claims and GARUDA speeds AIF approvals.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent SEBI tools and mechanisms?
o: GARUDA cuts approval for non-accredited investor schemes from 30 to 10 working days.
CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency.
Sudarshan is SEBI's in-house AI to monitor finfluencers.
x: NSE is the PaRRVA Data Centre; CARE Ratings is the PaRRVA Agency.

s: Who is the Chairperson of SEBI?
x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey heads SEBI, set up on 12 April 1988 and made statutory on 30 January 1992.

s: In which year did SEBI get statutory status?

s: Procurement of 20 lakh MT of potatoes under the Market Intervention Scheme was approved under which umbrella scheme?
x: The potato procurement was approved under PM-AASHA on a State's request.

s: How much did the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme receive in Budget 2026–27?
x: ECMS was allotted ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27; NITI Aayog has partnered Tata Electronics on electronics manufacturing.

s: What does VAANI, the AICTE initiative for technical education in Indian languages, stand for?
o: Vocational Advancement and Accreditation Network for Indian Education
Virtual Access for Academic Networks and New India
Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages
Vision for Applied Analytics and New Innovation
x: VAANI stands for Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages. The initiative focuses on advancing technical education through Indian languages.

s: From which date did sale of E20 petrol become mandatory at all petrol pumps across India?
x: E20 sale became mandatory at all petrol pumps from 1 April 2026; the EBP programme began in 2003.

s: The NITI Aayog–UNICEF India partnership on nutrition in aspirational districts is associated with which platform?
x: The partnership addresses nutrition and health in aspirational districts and blocks through the IMPAct4Nutrition platform.

s: Up to when did the CCEA extend the SARTHAK-PDS Central Scheme?
x: SARTHAK-PDS was extended to March 2031 with an outlay of ₹25,530 crore.

s: The Ministry of Culture signed an agreement with FICCI for which purpose?
o: Preparing a national electronics manufacturing strategy
Preparing a national nutrition and health strategy
Preparing a national cultural and creative economy strategy
x: The Ministry of Culture–FICCI agreement concerns a national cultural and creative economy strategy. Electronics manufacturing, nutrition and health, and pension services relate to other initiatives.

s: Which CBI initiative helps citizens verify CBI notices and curb digital arrest frauds?
x: Abhay is the CBI's AI chatbot for verifying CBI notices and curbing digital arrest frauds.

s: Which of the following about recent digital governance and market tools is NOT correct?
o: PRARAMBH, for the Income Tax Act 2025, includes the 'Kar Saathi' AI chatbot.

UIDAI's bug bounty programme concerns Aadhaar security.

s: Which body launched 'Arogya One' for planting medicinal plants along highways?
x: Arogya One is an NHAI initiative; phase 1 covers 17 locations, including in Andhra Pradesh.

s: The PRARAMBH income-tax awareness campaign from 1 April 2026 is for which new law that replaces the Act of 1961?
x: PRARAMBH spreads awareness of the Income Tax Act 2025, which replaces the 1961 Act; CBDT runs it with the 'Kar Saathi' chatbot.

s: Under which Act does the CBI work?
x: The CBI (1963) draws its legal powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.

s: Under which policy was the E20 petrol target set?
x: The E20 target (2025-26) comes from the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, amended in 2022; the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme began in 2003.

s: Which combination was identified as a driver of the renewed concern over zoonotic spillovers during the Hantavirus outbreak?
o: Deforestation, climate change, telemedicine and global travel
Deforestation, climate change, industrial livestock farming and global travel
Industrial livestock farming, geo-tagging, climate change and global travel
Deforestation, unpasteurised milk, industrial livestock farming and global travel

s: Where was SJVN, which is building the Lower Arun hydropower project in Nepal, established in 1988?
x: SJVN dates to 1988 at Shimla; Lower Arun is its second Nepal project after Arun-3.

s: What is the vector of the paddy dwarfing disease reported in Punjab?
x: The disease, caused by SRBSDV, is spread by the white-backed plant hopper and was first reported in Punjab in 2022.

s: India's first women SHG-managed solar plant (1 MW) at Venkatapuram is in which district of Telangana?
x: The 1 MW plant is at Venkatapuram in Khammam, linked to the Indira Mahila Shakti Scheme.

s: Which State ranked first under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm?
x: Telangana ranked first under NMEO-Oil Palm, which was launched in 2021.

s: Which of the following statements about the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park is incorrect?
o: It is the country's first PM MITRA Park at Warangal.

It is expected to generate 24,400 jobs.

s: The renewed Hantavirus outbreak highlighted zoonotic spillover through exposure to which materials from infected rodents?
o: Water or soil containing animal urine
x: Hantavirus spreads through the urine, droppings and saliva of infected rodents. Fleas on rodents are associated with plague, while water or soil with animal urine is linked to leptospirosis.

s: How does plague mainly spread to humans?
x: Plague spreads through fleas on rodents; Nipah via bats, pigs and fruit; brucellosis via cattle and milk; rabies via dogs and bats.

s: What is the capacity of SJVN's Lower Arun run-of-river project in Nepal?
x: Lower Arun is 679 MW; SJVN's earlier Nepal project Arun-3 is 900 MW.

s: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
x: The Koshi is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'; the Arun river of Nepal is its tributary.

x: The Kakatiya Mega Textile Park at Warangal (1,327 acres) is the country's first PM MITRA Park.
